BLOCK - security/292

Head: d398803f7169ef29f136704536205e8c8210ae06
Base: 27076a3793d62b8408b0a14aba89a569a710ad47
Request: 01a1f8fb-0cab-7560-b89e-ab6d5b0bd051

S292-001 - MEDIUM, confidence 9/10: a cross-user planted symlink redirects the socket-adjacent attach lock's permission change or file creation.

The new socket-adjacent lock can live in a directory writable by another OS account. Lock opening at crates/tmux/src/control.rs:647-654 uses O_WRONLY | O_CREAT and mode 0600, without O_NOFOLLOW, O_EXCL or O_TRUNC. It follows an existing symlink, inspects permissions on the opened descriptor and conditionally changes that descriptor's target to 0600 before taking its lock. It does not verify the descriptor's owner or regular-file type. Socket-parent selection at control.rs:595-619 does not enforce a trusted owner-only parent. The lock is taken at line 504, before tmux launches at lines 508-515.

Another UID able to plant the predictable lock name in such a parent can point it at a daemon-user-owned writable file. The daemon then changes that unrelated file's permissions to 0600: executable and group-access bits can be removed. A dangling link can instead cause creation of an empty 0600 target wherever the daemon user can create a file. These effects occur before tmux's later admission/refusal and before lock contention can reject the attach. A secure owner-only 0700 parent prevents planting, but is not enforced by this code; an observation that this machine's current default directory is private is not a guard for shared/custom parents.

This is introduced cross-user filesystem integrity/availability impact, not a hostile same-user scenario exempted by C33. No disclosure, content truncation, authentication bypass or privilege escalation is claimed.

Proof: an owned-temporary-fixture OS-primitive reproduction of the same open/fstat/fchmod/flock sequence changed a symlink target from 0755 to 0600 while preserving its bytes; following a dangling link created an empty 0600 target. Both assertions passed and the fixtures were removed. This verifies the filesystem effects, not a full production-adapter invocation or an actual second-UID execution. The complete 13-file exact-range source review establishes that the production lock takes this sequence.

Required repair: prevent symlink-directed opens atomically and do not narrow permissions on an unverified pre-existing object. Enforce the supported parent/object ownership and type invariant at the production lock boundary. Add a focused production-lock regression proving an unrelated symlink target's permissions/content and a dangling target remain untouched. A path-only symlink check followed by open is not a TOCTOU-safe repair.

Other security checks: the teardown if-shell format and branches are fixed literals, not external shell/format text; bounce PID arguments are quoted; the new signal handler introduces no cross-user signaling authority. No added credentials, private owner/name references or prohibited machine paths were identified. Changing the lock pathname does not itself establish mixed-old/new-version serialization; that operational proof remains with correctness review.

Validation: exact-head CI run 44737173992 succeeded. Rust job 136291370435 ran 2664 tests successfully, with 6 skipped overall. Successful-job artifact 14629142347, selected by ID from its upload log, proves pij-tmux control 32/32, adapter 41/41, control_mode 23/23 and control_teardown 4/4 passed, with no skips in those suites. Both Node 22 and Node 24 CI jobs passed typecheck, lint, npm test and native Copilot contracts. These green tests do not cover S292-001.

The alone/off mutants and full crash-count experiments were not independently rerun by security. The correctness reviewer owns its targeted branch and adapter proofs. Performance's separate BLOCK at 6f069620dfa17233b28b1a567e6b081776510290 covers the unbounded pipe-write path and bounce cost/time qualifications; this security finding does not duplicate those findings or clear them for merge.

Local validation: harness checks --json completed at 2026-11-20T12:52:53Z with exit 1. Its Rust workspace fmt/clippy/tests, route-inventory, smoke, pij-skill, native Copilot and Copilot SDK stages passed. The eight failed stages were local-paths, omp-config, ddocs, coverage, typecheck, lockfile, lint and test: local TS tooling was missing, and the ambient Biome did not understand the repository's v2 configuration. Attribution was an advisory warning. No heavy sensor was skipped. The overall local gate is not green, and is not represented as ship-ready; exact-head CI is the separate TS proof. No dependencies were installed or linked to repair the read-only review environment.

Holding security/292 remains until merge. This is a read-only review; no product source, installed daemon or live tmux server was modified.

Harness feedback: lock relocation preserved a permission-narrowing mechanism while changing its parent-directory trust boundary. The highest-leverage encoding is the actual production-lock symlink regression above, rather than a prose assurance that locks are private. Dependency-free review readiness remains separately qualified under C25; no node_modules was installed or linked.
